orange-tabby: The substantial rectangular torso, sturdy moderate legs, oval adult face, amber eyes, cream ventral areas, and long ringed tail remain recognizable in all six poses.
The cat stays fuller and heavier than the Li Hua without becoming round-headed or British-cobby.
Forehead, cheek, neck, flank, leg, and tail marking families remain stable under pose foreshortening.
li-hua: The long legs, narrow waist, defined shoulder blades, long neck, wedge-leaning face, large ears, yellow-green eyes, and active tail remain recognizable in all six poses.
The Li Hua remains visibly leaner, taller, and more angular than the orange tabby; it is not a recolor of the orange anatomy.
The dark forehead M, cheek bars, butterfly shoulder region, narrow flank bars, barred legs, and strongly ringed tail remain stable under pose foreshortening.

sit: Both cats have grounded pelvises and paired load-bearing forepaws beneath the shoulders.
The orange sit reads broad and sturdy; the Li Hua sit reads tall, narrow, and long-legged.
sleep: Both cats show chest and belly compression against the resting plane, heads supported by forepaws, tucked hindquarters, and tails attached at the sacrum.
The orange rest forms a fuller oval; the Li Hua rest retains a longer, more angular crescent.
walk: Each walk-ready pose has three grounded load-bearing paws and one low advancing forepaw.
Spines, wrists, hocks, shoulder placement, belly suspension, and counterbalancing tails are plausible.
The Li Hua has visibly longer limbs and stronger scapular definition than the orange tabby.
eat: Both cats use a four-foot crouch with flexed elbows and hocks, raised shoulder blades, and a lowered neck reaching a correctly scaled bowl.
No paw, muzzle, or tail penetrates the bowl.
play: Both poses retain planted hind paws, a supporting forepaw, a reaching forepaw, focused eyes, and a sacrum-attached balancing tail.
Each yarn ball is isolated as the only interaction prop and does not hide or substitute for a limb.
gaze: The orange cat uses a grounded upright seated gaze; the Li Hua uses a grounded rear-three-quarter standing gaze.
The differing gaze silhouettes reinforce that the cats were independently posed rather than recolored from one base.

styleFindings: Color grading is low-saturation and compatible with the approved warm paper, sage, and wood room palette.
Edges use partially transparent feathering and warm brown-gray definition rather than a hard vector cutout.

Fine fur and stripe rendering is somewhat more detailed than the softest areas of the approved room wash, but remains within a watercolor candidate direction and is intentionally left for visual approval.
scaleFindings: Both sleep poses were composited with the approved home v3 room at the existing Minho 420 px portrait canvas rect and bottom-center anchor.
At 390×844 and 430×932 the cats rest on the woven rug without a visible gap, penetration, or need for a separate contact shadow.
The orange tabby reads fuller at the same anchor; the Li Hua reads leaner while retaining plausible adult body length.
technicalFindings: All twelve masters are 1024×1024 sRGB RGBA PNGs with at least 64 px safe margin.
All twelve runtime-review derivatives are 512×512 sRGB RGBA PNGs.
Fully transparent pixels have zero RGB and every master retains partially transparent edge pixels.
Source files contain no text, UI, scenery, floor patch, baked shadow, border, or watermark.
knownReviewPoints: Count individual mackerel bars by anatomical region rather than demanding identical visible counts in foreshortened or occluded poses.
Judge whether the remaining fine fur detail should be softened further before any later production pass.
The gaze silhouettes intentionally differ: orange is seated while Li Hua is standing and actively balanced.
